own_tests.input: Row-by-row comparison of the new extra_train.csv with the T4.5 version, plus uniqueness and group-namespace checks
own_tests.result: 0 of 3,347 old rows changed; 137 new rows with the claimed class split; 3,484 unique paths and sha1s; 0 group overlap with field and lab.

own_tests.input: Independent crop, zoom and rotation-tolerant search that uses none of the builder's methods (no hashes, no 32x32 correlation, no DINOv2, no ORB): normalised cross-correlation template matching (skimage match_template) of a central 50% patch of each of the 137 rows against all 291 apple-class field_dev and field_test photos at scales 0.7, 1.0 and 1.4, over 8 rotations and flips, and the reverse direction at scale 1.0. Run on all 137 rows.
own_tests.result: Highest scores 0.93 down to 0.885. I viewed the top 36 distinct pairs as montages: none is a copy. The top hits are low-texture stock leaves on white, or different orchard leaves against apple fruit, black rot or rust photos.

own_tests.input: Positive control for that search, built from a 70% crop of 4 field_test apple photos, also rotated 90 degrees
own_tests.result: Same-photo scores 0.88 to 0.96 against 0.35 to 0.74 for an unrelated photo, with the rotated copy scoring the same. So the method finds crops and rotations. It is not perfect: the weakest control (0.877) would fall below the 0.93 top non-copy scores, which is why I viewed 36 pairs instead of relying on a threshold. (My first control attempt was mis-scaled and showed no separation; that was a bug in my control, fixed in the second run.)

own_tests.input: Leak search limited to the apple classes of field_dev and field_test (291 photos), because the 137 rows are apple only
own_tests.result: Not run against the non-apple dev/test classes with my method. The builder's ORB search and the pipeline's correlation and DINOv2 checks did cover all 2,075 photos.

own_tests.input: Read the ORB logs for gaps at the restart seam
own_tests.result: Query ids 0-88 in orb.log and 89-137 in orb2.log are contiguous, with no duplicates or missing ids.

notes: For T4.6 and later work, lesser gaps, none of which block T4.8. (1) The ORB script (leak_orb.py), its logs and the control crop are in a scratchpad and not committed, so the independent leak search is not reproducible from the repo. (2) Only 137 of 11,310 mapped rows survive. The crop check dropped 3,530, almost all by class-token cosine >= 0.80 with an apple dev/test photo. The builder viewed 12 flagged pairs and none was a copy, so the rule over-removes. The survivors are the rows least like the field apple photos, which is selection bias. (3) 106 Apple scab rows come from one orchard and camera style, while Apple healthy has none from this source (its 200 are PlantWild web photos). A style shortcut for scab versus healthy is possible, so read E12's Apple scab confusions and compare scab with and without the PP rows. (4) The rust mapping to Apple___Cedar_apple_rust is an inference, and 4 of 24 viewed samples showed only tiny spots, so rust may include other rusts. (5) The mirror's license is unconfirmed: weights trained on it need the person's check before publishing. (6) Known blind spots: copies with no texture in common, and copies rotated by 90 degrees, are caught only at full frame by correlation. My template search does handle 90-degree rotation and found nothing, but it has limited power on low-texture photos. (7) The per-step drop counts for the new rows are differences between builds, not logged per source. (8) pyarrow was added to pyproject.toml, which is reasonable for reading parquet. (9) The first two ORB logs are in a scratchpad directory shared with other tasks.
